category: Financial Inclusion, Government Financial Schemes, and Basic Financial Services
title: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY): Zero-Balance, Overdraft & ₹2 Lakh RuPay Cover
questions: What are the benefits of a Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) account?
What is the overdraft limit in a Jan Dhan account?
Does a Jan Dhan RuPay debit card provide free accidental insurance?
Can anyone open a PMJDY account in India?
content: The world's largest financial inclusion initiative launched by the Government of India: (1) Core Benefits: Universal access to banking with zero minimum balance requirement, free RuPay debit card, and direct benefit transfer (DBT) integration for all government welfare subsidies. (2) Built-in Accidental Insurance: Free accidental death/disability insurance cover of ₹2,00,000 on RuPay cards issued to accounts opened after August 2018 (provided the card was used at least once in the previous 90 days). (3) Overdraft Facility: Overdraft facility up to ₹10,000 sanctioned to eligible account holders (one per household, preferably the lady of the house) without collateral.
source: Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance - PMJDY Guidelines

category: Financial Inclusion, Government Financial Schemes, and Basic Financial Services
title: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY): ₹2 Lakh Life Cover for ₹436/Year
questions: What is Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)?
How much is the annual premium for PMJJBY?
What is the eligibility age for PMJJBY?
Does PMJJBY cover death due to any cause including disease?
content: Government-backed pure term life insurance scheme providing affordable protection: (1) Eligibility: All bank and post-office savings account holders aged 18 to 50 years. Risk coverage ceases at age 55. (2) Premium: Fixed annual premium of ₹436 per annum, automatically debited in one instalment from the subscriber's bank account in May every year. (3) Death Benefit: Pays ₹2,00,000 (Rupees Two Lakh) to the nominee upon the death of the insured due to ANY reason (illness, disease, heart attack, or accident). (4) Simple Enrolment: Zero medical screening; simple auto-debit consent form.
source: Ministry of Finance - Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) Rules

category: Financial Inclusion, Government Financial Schemes, and Basic Financial Services
title: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY): ₹2 Lakh Accidental Cover for ₹20/Year
questions: What is Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)?
What is the annual premium for PMSBY?
What is the difference between PMJJBY and PMSBY?
Does PMSBY cover natural death from illness?
content: Government-backed personal accident insurance scheme offering mass protection: (1) Eligibility: All bank and post-office account holders aged 18 to 70 years. (2) Premium: Highly subsidised premium of only ₹20 per annum, automatically debited in May. (3) Benefits: (a) ₹2,00,000 for accidental death or total irreversible loss of both eyes or loss of both hands/feet, (b) ₹1,00,000 for partial permanent disability (loss of sight of one eye or loss of one hand/foot). (4) Crucial Distinction: PMSBY covers death or disability resulting SOLELY from accidents; it does NOT cover natural death from illnesses or diseases.
source: Ministry of Finance - Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) Rules

category: Financial Inclusion, Government Financial Schemes, and Basic Financial Services
title: Atal Pension Yojana (APY): Guaranteed ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 Monthly Pension from Age 60
questions: What is Atal Pension Yojana (APY)?
How much monthly pension is guaranteed under APY?
Who is eligible to join Atal Pension Yojana?
Can income-tax payers join Atal Pension Yojana?
content: Government guaranteed pension scheme administered by PFRDA targeted at unorganized sector workers: (1) Eligibility: Indian citizens aged 18 to 40 holding a savings bank account (income-tax payers are barred from joining since Oct 2022). (2) Guaranteed Pension Tiers: Subscribers choose a fixed monthly pension of ₹1,000, ₹2,000, ₹3,000, ₹4,000, or ₹5,000 per month starting from age 60 until death. Monthly contributions depend on joining age. (3) Triple Benefit: (a) Guaranteed pension to subscriber for life, (b) Upon subscriber demise, same pension continues to spouse for life, (c) Upon demise of both, entire accumulated pension corpus returns to nominees.
source: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) - Atal Pension Yojana Scheme Details

title: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY): High Interest, 21-Year Tenure & Section 80C Exemption
questions: What is Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY)?
What is the maximum age of girl child to open an SSY account?
Is Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana interest tax-free?
When can money be withdrawn from an SSY account?
content: Special small-savings scheme under the 'Beti Bachao Beti Padhao' campaign: (1) Eligibility: Opened by parents/guardians for a girl child from birth up to age 10 (maximum 2 accounts per family, with twins/triplets exception). (2) High Interest & EEE Tax Status: Offers one of the highest government small-savings interest rates (typically 8.2% p.a., compounded annually). Complete EEE tax status: Section 80C deduction on deposits, tax-free annual interest, and 100% tax-free maturity payout. (3) Maturity: Matures 21 years from account opening. Partial withdrawal up to 50% permitted after age 18 for higher education.
source: Ministry of Finance - Sukanya Samriddhi Account Rules 2019

category: Financial Inclusion, Government Financial Schemes, and Basic Financial Services
title: Public Provident Fund (PPF): 15-Year EEE Sovereign Scheme & Sovereign Immunity
questions: What is Public Provident Fund (PPF)?
How long is the lock-in period for PPF?
Can PPF balance be attached by a court or creditors?
What is the minimum and maximum deposit in PPF per year?
content: Flagship 15-year long-term savings instrument operated under the Government Savings Promotion Act: (1) Financial Limits: Minimum deposit ₹500, maximum ₹1,50,000 per financial year. Interest is set quarterly by the Ministry of Finance and compounded annually. (2) Triple Exempt (EEE): Principal qualifies for Section 80C, interest is completely tax-free, and maturity payout is 100% exempt from income tax. (3) Immunity from Court Attachment: Under statutory law, the balance in a PPF account cannot be attached by any court decree or creditors against debts or liabilities. (4) Extensions: Can be extended in blocks of 5 years indefinitely with or without further contributions.
source: Public Provident Fund Scheme 2019 & Ministry of Finance Notifications

category: Financial Inclusion, Government Financial Schemes, and Basic Financial Services
title: Senior Citizens Savings Scheme (SCSS): ₹30 Lakh Cap, Quarterly Interest Payouts
questions: What is Senior Citizens Savings Scheme (SCSS)?
What is the maximum investment limit in SCSS?
How often is interest paid in Senior Citizens Savings Scheme?
Is SCSS investment eligible for Section 80C tax deduction?
content: Government-backed retirement income scheme for senior citizens: (1) Eligibility: Individuals aged 60 years and above (or 55+ for individuals who retired under VRS within 1 month of receiving retirement benefits; 50+ for retired defence personnel). (2) Investment Limit: Up to ₹30,00,000 (increased from ₹15 Lakh in Budget 2023). (3) Tenure & Payouts: 5-year tenure (extendable by 3 years). Pays guaranteed government interest quarterly directly into the retiree's savings account. (4) Tax Treatment: Investment eligible for Section 80C up to ₹1.5 Lakh. Quarterly interest is taxable, eligible for Section 80TTB deduction up to ₹50,000.
source: Ministry of Finance - Senior Citizens Savings Scheme Rules 2019

category: Financial Inclusion, Government Financial Schemes, and Basic Financial Services
title: Mahila Samman Savings Certificate (MSSC): 7.5% Interest, 2-Year Deposit for Women
questions: What is Mahila Samman Savings Certificate (MSSC)?
What is the interest rate on Mahila Samman Certificate?
What is the maximum deposit in Mahila Samman scheme?
Can a man open a Mahila Samman account?
content: Dedicated small-savings initiative launched by the Central Government to commemorate Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav: (1) Exclusivity: Can be opened exclusively by women or by a guardian on behalf of a minor girl child at post offices and designated commercial banks. (2) Financial Terms: Fixed tenure of 2 years; maximum deposit limit of ₹2,00,000 (minimum ₹1,000). (3) Interest Rate: Attractive fixed interest rate of 7.5% per annum, compounded quarterly and credited at maturity. (4) Partial Withdrawal: Allows a partial withdrawal of up to 40% of the balance after 1 year to meet emergency requirements.
source: Ministry of Finance - Mahila Samman Savings Certificate Scheme 2023

category: Financial Inclusion, Government Financial Schemes, and Basic Financial Services
title: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana: Shishu, Kishor & Tarun Collateral-Free Business Loans
questions: What is Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY)?
What are the 3 categories of MUDRA loans?
Do MUDRA loans require collateral or property security?
What is the maximum limit for a MUDRA loan?
content: Financial inclusion credit architecture providing micro-funding to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises: (1) Three Funding Categories: (a) Shishu: Loans up to ₹50,000 (for new micro ventures), (b) Kishor: Loans between ₹50,000 and ₹5,00,000, and (c) Tarun: Loans between ₹5,00,000 and ₹10,00,000 (limit increased to ₹20,00,000 for entrepreneurs who previously took and repaid Tarun loans). (2) Zero Collateral: Banks and NBFCs are strictly prohibited from demanding third-party guarantors or property collateral for MUDRA loans; credit guarantees are backed by CGFMU.
source: Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency (MUDRA) Guidelines & DFS Ministry of Finance

category: Financial Inclusion, Government Financial Schemes, and Basic Financial Services
title: PM SVANidhi: Micro-Credit for Urban Street Vendors with Interest Subsidies
questions: What is PM SVANidhi scheme for street vendors?
How much loan can a street vendor get under PM SVANidhi?
What is the interest subsidy in PM SVANidhi?
How does digital transaction cashback work in PM SVANidhi?
content: Special micro-credit facility launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs to empower urban street vendors: (1) Tiered Loan Tranches: Initial working capital loan of ₹10,000 repayable in 12 months. Upon timely repayment, borrowers graduate to a second tranche of ₹20,000 and a third tranche of ₹50,000. (2) 7% Interest Subsidy: Timely loan repayment triggers an interest subsidy of 7% per annum credited directly to the vendor's bank account. (3) Digital Cashbacks: Vendors receive monthly cashbacks up to ₹100 for conducting digital transactions via QR codes, building formal credit histories.
source: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs - PM SVANidhi Portal Guidelines

category: Financial Inclusion, Government Financial Schemes, and Basic Financial Services
title: Stand-Up India Scheme: ₹10 Lakh to ₹1 Crore Green-Field Enterprise Financing
questions: What is the Stand-Up India scheme?
Who is eligible for loans under Stand-Up India?
What is the loan amount range under Stand-Up India?
What kind of businesses are funded by Stand-Up India?
content: Enterprise financing architecture supporting grassroots entrepreneurship: (1) Mandate: Every scheduled commercial bank branch must facilitate at least one SC/ST borrower and at least one woman borrower to establish a greenfield enterprise. (2) Funding Quantum: Composite loans (term loan and working capital) between ₹10,00,000 and ₹1,00,00,000. (3) Eligible Sectors: Manufacturing, services, trading, and agri-allied activities. The borrower must hold at least 51% shareholding and controlling stake in the enterprise.
source: Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance - Stand-Up India Guidelines

category: Financial Inclusion, Government Financial Schemes, and Basic Financial Services
title: Kisan Vikas Patra (KVP) & National Savings Certificate (NSC): Post Office Fixed Growth
questions: What is the difference between KVP and NSC?
How long does it take for money to double in Kisan Vikas Patra?
Does National Savings Certificate (NSC) offer Section 80C tax deduction?
Can KVP and NSC certificates be pledged for bank loans?
content: Government-backed small-savings certificates available through India Post and authorized banks: (1) Kisan Vikas Patra (KVP): A capital-doubling scheme with a sovereign guarantee. Doubles your investment over a fixed notified tenure (typically 115 months depending on prevailing interest rates). Transferable between holders; interest is taxable. (2) National Savings Certificate (NSC): 5-year fixed maturity instrument. Deposits qualify for tax deduction under Section 80C. Interest accrued annually is deemed reinvested and also qualifies for 80C in the first 4 years. Both certificates can be pledged with banks as collateral for loans.
source: National Savings Certificates (VIII Issue) Rules & KVP Rules 2019
